newsitem.title: JORDAN: Amman bourse lower but close to three year high.
newsitem.headline: Amman bourse lower but close to three year high.

text.p: Jordan's bourse was a touch lower on Sunday as investors took a pause a day after a buying spree on Arab Bank sent the official index soaring to new three-year highs.

Arab Bank's stock fell one dinar to close at 295 dinars on investor dismay after the cabinet again delayed endorsing a recommendation announced at the start of the month by the state's top investment body to scrap foreign ownership ceilings.

Market confidence has been bolstered since the decision was announced amid widespread expectations it would result in renewed global fund buying on blue-chips which had reached an existing 50 percent ownership ceiling.

Mostly local investor demand along with some foreign inspired buying in Arab Bank has almost single-handedly pushed the official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index to its highest level since March 1994.
Arab Bank's 10 dinar jump on Saturday was mainly fuelled by expectations the cabinet would announce its approval of the move at its regular session that day.
The official 60 share index shed 0.08 percent to 167.61 points on Sunday.
Arab Bank again dominated trade, accounting for nearly half of the one million dinar turnover.

Arab Bank shares are at a five-year high and the market's official index -- highly sensitive to moves in the price of the stock which accounts for almost one third of the Amman bourse's 3.4 billion dinar capitalisation -- has matched their gains.
Brokers continue to attribute the bank's popularity to forecasts of strong 1997 profits, expectations of a bonus share offering, and government plans to scrap foreign share ownership ceilings.
The second busiest share was Jordan Islamic Bank, which rose 0.02 dinars to 3.91 dinars in turnover worth 199,005 dinars. $1 = 0.709 dinars
